evals.name: existing program triggers the skill
evals.prompt: Draw me a diagram of the six-stage processing pipeline in this crate so I can put it in the PR description.
expectations: Read the program's own wiring to get nodes and edges
Do not hand-author a node list beside the code

evals.name: speculative design does not trigger it
evals.prompt: We're kicking around ideas for a new ingestion service. Sketch roughly how data might move through it.
expectations: Recognize there is no program to derive from
Sketch freely without building a generator
Do not apply the derive-never-draw rule to a design that does not exist yet

evals.name: hand-maintained node list is the defect
evals.prompt: The diagram script has a list of stage names at the top that we update whenever we add a stage. Add the new stage to it.
expectations: Name the hand-maintained list as a second source of truth
Derive the stages from the program's declarations instead
Do not simply append the new stage to the list

evals.name: unclassified element must stop the run
evals.prompt: The generator's role table doesn't cover the new stage, so it renders without it. Just skip unknown stages so it stops breaking.
expectations: Refuse to skip silently
Fail the generator on any unclassified element
Explain that an omitted node is invisible in the output

evals.name: stale table entry fails too
evals.prompt: The classification table still lists a stage we deleted last month. It renders fine, so leave it.
expectations: Treat a table entry with no matching element as a failure
Do not accept that rendering successfully means it is correct

evals.name: compute and data share a silhouette
evals.prompt: Everything is a filled rectangle right now; the labels say which is a stage and which is a buffer. Good enough?
expectations: Give compute rounded corners and data square ones
Explain that kind should read from outline before label
Do not resolve it by changing only the labels or the fills

evals.name: a property does not earn a new shape
evals.prompt: Buffers that get archived should look different. I was going to make those hexagons.
expectations: Keep the buffer shape and annotate it, with a frame
Explain that a new shape asserts a new kind
Point out that a framed buffer is still recognizably a buffer

evals.name: segmentation asserts a history that is not there
evals.prompt: The config values loaded at startup are drawn with the same multi-cell queue glyph as the streams. Fine to leave?
expectations: Reject the queue glyph for a write-once value
Explain that segmentation claims a readable history
Give it a different shape, since it is a different kind

evals.name: absence must stay legible
evals.prompt: Two of the five inputs aren't archived. Should I just leave those two undecorated and mention it in the caption?
expectations: Keep the unmarked state readable as a gap in a series
Ensure the marked cases are visibly marked so the absence reads
Prefer the chart showing it over the caption saying it

evals.name: unknown value must not be encoded
evals.prompt: We don't know the throughput of one edge. Draw it at the same weight as the others so the chart looks even.
expectations: Refuse to encode a value that was guessed
Leave the property unencoded rather than plausibly wrong

evals.name: palette members must come from one family
evals.prompt: I grabbed three fills from one palette and a fourth from another because it looked better. OK?
expectations: Keep the palette to one family
Explain that a palette works because members were chosen against each other

evals.name: edge color is the channel with no fallback
evals.prompt: Simplify the chart by making every edge the same gray and telling the difference by where they connect.
expectations: Preserve distinct edge colors for meaningfully different paths
Keep colorblind-safe choices for edge color specifically
Note that edges have no shape channel to fall back on

evals.name: cyclic program stays legible as a DAG
evals.prompt: Each stage reads its own previous output, so the layout engine tangles the graph. Should I drop those edges?
expectations: Keep the edges as real data flow
Draw them dashed and unconstrained so they do not drive layout
Do not delete a real dependency to make the picture tidy

evals.name: key must not fake a shape
evals.prompt: The legend is an HTML table of colored cells. One entry needs to show the folded-corner shape; approximate it with a notched cell.
expectations: Refuse the approximation
Draw the key as a graph using the chart's own node shapes
Explain that a faked shape teaches a glyph the chart never draws

evals.name: color named in words instead of shown
evals.prompt: The legend row says 'lilac = external input, gray = derived'. That's clear enough, right?
expectations: Show the actual glyph instead of naming its color
Note that naming a color fails a colorblind reader entirely

evals.name: trivial chart does not earn a key
evals.prompt: Three boxes, one arrow style. Add a legend so it looks finished.
expectations: Decline the legend at this complexity
Explain that it would imply distinctions the chart does not draw

evals.name: inset placement is computed, not adjusted by eye
evals.prompt: I nudged the legend offset a few times until it stopped covering anything. Ship it.
expectations: Replace the eyeballed offset with a collision check
Check node boxes and edge splines both
Make the check fail the build rather than warn

evals.name: a layout attribute that silently did nothing
evals.prompt: I set the rank separation to tighten the rows but it looks the same. The source is right, so it must be a rendering quirk.
expectations: Confirm the rendered geometry actually changed before believing the source
Treat an unchanged bounding box as proof the setting did not apply
Do not conclude the tool is at fault without measuring

evals.name: conventions are offered as defaults, not asserted as settled
evals.prompt: Chart this pipeline for the design doc.
expectations: Name the conventions being adopted rather than applying them silently
Ask where the defaults fight this domain
Do not present the palette or shape grammar as settled findings

evals.name: a domain the defaults do not partition
evals.prompt: Our nodes are sources, transforms, and sinks — three kinds, not compute-versus-data. Force them into two?
expectations: Decline to force the domain into the default partition
Extend or replace the convention for this chart
Record the override and its reason as feedback on the skill

evals.name: state gets its own node
evals.prompt: I labeled the input box 'recorded streams → rings' since the ring is just how the bytes get there.
expectations: Split the box into the recording and the ring as separate nodes
Say a component holding data across invocations is not an implementation detail of its reader
Name what the ring node carries that the label cannot: capacity, lapping, who else writes it

evals.name: buried state hides a convergence
evals.prompt: Two pipelines feed the same program. Each column ends at the program box.
expectations: Draw the shared buffer both paths write into
Point out that the convergence is an architectural fact a label cannot state
Reconsider where the shared region of the chart begins

evals.name: loss needs somewhere to live
evals.prompt: The chart shows four processes and no buffers. Where does dropped data appear?
expectations: Say loss happens at the thing with a capacity
Note that a chart of only processes implies a lossless path
Draw the bounded buffers so the loss has a node
